new_findings_today.title: refresh-stay-picks-agent's nightly destination-selection logic is stuck re-processing the same ~15-20 thin-lodging destinations, leaving ~82% of the catalog (435/533 destinations) untouched for 14+ days
new_findings_today.detail: This was first surfaced by the job itself on 2026-09-12 and confirmed persisting again in its 2026-09-13T22:27:52Z run (self-reported via ops_reports.summary.selection_loop_finding, not something this QA session tested directly, but treated as in-scope supplementary evidence the same way this skill has tracked the job's egress block since 08-19). Root cause per the job's own analysis: many destinations have 1-3 of their 4 stay-pick slots that can never get a real, verifiable answer (forest rest-houses, pilgrimage towns with no distinct hotels, day-trip sites with zero on-site lodging). Because the selection query sorts by MIN(refreshed_at) across all 4 slots, an old, permanently-unfillable slot anchors that destination near the top of the nightly 20-destination selection indefinitely, regardless of how many times its fillable slots get reconfirmed. 13 of the 20 destinations in the 09-13 batch were also processed on both 09-11 and 09-12. The job itself is not fabricating data to route around this -- it correctly returns honest scarcity for the unfillable slots each time -- but the practical effect is that most of the catalog is going stale from a freshness standpoint while a small, recurring set gets re-verified nightly.
new_findings_today.evidence: ops_reports row for job='refresh-stay-picks-agent', run_at='2026-09-13 22:27:52.753464+00': summary.selection_loop_finding states '13 of tonight's 20 selected destinations... were also processed on 2026-09-11 AND 2026-09-12 -- the exact bug the 2026-09-12 run flagged... of 533 total destinations, only 7 have ANY slot touched in the last 2 days, and 435 (82%) have a stale slot older than 14 days.' The prior run (2026-09-12T22:25:45Z) independently reports the same root cause and an equivalent 435-destination staleness count.
new_findings_today.recommendation: A selection-logic change is needed, as the job itself recommends: either track a destination-level last_checked_at independent of per-slot refreshed_at, or exclude destinations whose unfillable slots are already flagged as honest, permanent scarcity from the stalest-first sort. This is a founder/engineering decision on the job's selection query, not something the nightly job should silently work around -- flagging it into the QA regression matrix so it doesn't quietly recur unnoticed the way the egress block did for weeks before being tracked here.
